- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model shows mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the forecast window; reduce first 5–7 days by 1–2% if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model fails to correct; add a downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.12) over 5+ days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days to avoid “sentiment lag” error.
